sketches.mechanism: The Maybe monad's bind operator silently propagates Nothing, so once absence enters a chain, every subsequent step yields Nothing without ever being evaluated.
sketches.resonance: Once someone is gone, every future you imagined with them collapses untouched.
sketches.draft:
future :: Maybe a -> Maybe b -> Maybe c -> Maybe (a, b, c)
future you me us = do
  y <- you
  m <- me
  u <- us
  return (y, m, u)

-- future (Just _) Nothing _ == Nothing

sketches.mechanism: Ruby's frozen? method and freeze: once an object is frozen, any attempt to modify it raises a RuntimeError. The object persists but can never change again.
sketches.resonance: Some versions of yourself survive perfectly intact — and that is exactly the damage.
sketches.draft:
yesterday = self.dup.freeze

yesterday.frozen?  # => true

begin
  yesterday.grow
rescue => e
  retry
end

sketches.mechanism: A sealed trait with a single case object means pattern matching is exhaustive with only one possibility — the compiler knows there is nothing else.
sketches.resonance: When you've eliminated every other explanation, the one that remains — however unbearable — is the truth.
